about: The scanner couldn't log in, so it guessed the version from a banner. Distros backport fixes without changing that version, so these need a person; with a working login the same check is trustworthy.

cases.why: Ubuntu backported the fix; the banner still says 8.9p1. Known limitation: without a login the rules can't see the backport, so this goes to review (counts against recall).

findings.title: OpenSSH < 9.6 Multiple Vulnerabilities
findings.description: According to its banner, the version of OpenSSH running on the remote host is prior to 9.6.
findings.plugin_output:
Version source : SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_8.9p1 Ubuntu-3ubuntu0.10
Installed version : 8.9p1
Fixed version : 9.6

cases.why: Qualys potential, from a distro-suffixed banner.

findings.title: OpenSSH Multiple Vulnerabilities
findings.result: Vulnerable SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_8.9p1 Ubuntu-3ubuntu0.10 detected on port 22 over TCP.

cases.why: Login configured but failed on this host; the version check fell back to the banner.

findings.title: Nginx Multiple Vulnerabilities
findings.result: Vulnerable version of Nginx detected on port 443 - 1.18.0

cases.why: Same kind of check with a working login reads the installed package.

findings.title: Nginx Multiple Vulnerabilities
findings.result: Vulnerable version of Nginx detected on port 443 - 1.18.0

cases.why: Qualys names the check itself as an unauthenticated detection, even in a login scan.

findings.title: OpenSSL Multiple Vulnerabilities (Unauthenticated Detection)
findings.result: Vulnerable OpenSSL version detected on port 443.

cases.why: Credentialed local check read the package database: installed is below the fix.

findings.title: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS : OpenSSH vulnerabilities (USN-0001-1)
findings.plugin_output:
Remote package installed : openssh-server_1:8.9p1-3ubuntu0.4
Should be : openssh-server_1:8.9p1-3ubuntu0.6

cases.why: A TLS setting is observed directly; no login or version needed.
